title: Expose bare kinetic fluctuations hidden by a small helical momentum
statement: For the complete live-lead helical Gibbs family, (pY/(g hbar sqrt b),L/(hbar sqrt b)) converges in distribution to(-G,G), Var(G)=1/2. Truncated-square positivity gives liminf<pY^2>/(g^2 hbar^2 b)>=1/2 and liminf<L^2>/(hbar^2 b)>=1/2. Bare kinetic lower orders grow as R log R for logarithmic b and R^2 log^2 R for b=R log^2 R.

requires: Complete fixed-I,B0 live-lead model and preceding actual Gibbs comparison; growing gain and either declared b family; actual physical momentum pY=P-gL.
provides: For the complete live-lead helical Gibbs family, (pY/(g hbar sqrt b),L/(hbar sqrt b)) converges in distribution to(-G,G), Var(G)=1/2. Truncated-square positivity gives liminf<pY^2>/(g^2 hbar^2 b)>=1/2 and liminf<L^2>/(hbar^2 b)>=1/2. Bare kinetic lower orders grow as R log R for logarithmic b and R^2 log^2 R for b=R log^2 R.
assumptions: Only lower semicontinuity of second moments is established, not convergence. This is equilibrium kinetic fluctuation, not heat dissipated per use, universal work cost or a lower bound on every nonlinear mechanical implementation.
costs: The logarithmic lock has bare translational kinetic lower orderR logR; the stronger dynamical lock has R^2log^2R. Real material rigidity, velocity and bandwidth ceilings need their own measured model.
contract.units: pY is linear momentum, L is angular momentum, g inverse length. Scaled limits are dimensionless; T_bare=pY^2/(2B0)+L^2/(2I) is energy.
contract.obstruction: Bounded Cartesian rotor position and a small helical P do not imply bounded actual kinetic resources.

body: Use the W0 product comparison only for bounded measurements; the exact Bessel characteristic of exp(b cos psi) and Gaussian helical P give the joint weak limit. The actual identity pY=P-gL converts it to physical momenta. Apply min(x^2,K), take the gain limit, then K to infinity. This avoids inferring unbounded moment convergence from vanishing trace distance. Opposite large bare momenta cancel in P; the actual bare-mass f-sum remains fixed with spectral weight outside the scaled thermal window.
